sentences.text:
This Appeal Coming On For Further Hearing This
Day, The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

In this appeal the appellant-Insurance Company has challenged the judgment dated 30.07.2011 passed in M.V.C.No.100/2009 by the Fast Track Court-II, Koppal (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal', for short).

2. The appellant-Insurance Company was the third respondent, respondents No.1 to 3 were the legal representatives of deceased petitioner and second respondent before the Tribunal was the owner of the vehicle.
The owner-third respondent is not made party to this appeal, as the Insurance Company has accepted its liability to indemnify the owner.
The parties will be NC: 2024:KHC-D:7967 referred to with respect to their status before the Tribunal for the sake of convenience.

3. Briefly stated, the facts are that, on 18.02.2008, the original petitioner Hanumantha Gouda was riding the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA- 37/L-5952, as a pillion rider, which was riding by Sankappa Sangati.

At about 4.00 pm on Koppal-Kushtagi Road, near Lebageri village, a Tom Tom 3 wheeler bearing registration No.KA-26/TR-1720 came from the opposite direction and caused the accident, due to which the rider of the motorcycle died at the spot and Hanumantha Gouda suffered injuries.

He was treated at Government Hospital, Koppal and SDM Medical College and Hospital,
Dharwad, under hospitalization.

entities.text:
SDM Medical College and Hospital,
Dharwad
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 4. After taking treatment, Hanumantha Gouda approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation of Rs.21,50,000/-.
The claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.

During the pendancy of the Iffco Tokio General Insurance Co., Ltd vs Hanumantha Gouda S/O. Sangana Gouda on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73282535/
2 claim petition, Hanumantha Gouda died leaving behind his legal heirs, NC: 2024:KHC-D:7967 wife and sons, who are the respondents herein in this appeal.

entities.text: Iffco Tokio General Insurance Co., Ltd vs Hanumantha Gouda S/O. Sangana Gouda
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The legal representatives of Hanumantha Gouda have prosecuted the claim petition on the ground that Hanumantha Gouda died on account of injuries sustained in the accident and they being the dependents entitled to claim compensation.

The Tribunal, after taking the evidence and hearing both sides, awarded compensation of Rs.6,70,802/- with interest at 6% p.a., directing the owner and the insurer of the Tom Tom to pay the compensation.
Aggrieved by the same, the Insurance Company has filed this appeal on various grounds.

5. Heard the arguments of Sri. Ravindra R. Mane, learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company and Sri. Deepak S. Maganur, learned counsel for respondents No.1 to 3.
6.
It is the contention of learned counsel for the Insurance Company that, the accident took place on 18.02.2008 and Hanumantha Gouda died on 25.02.2009.

Hanumantha Gouda was inpatient at Government Hospital, NC: 2024:KHC-D:7967 Koppal as well as the SDM Medical Hospital,
Dharwad, for a period of two months.
He has suffered only fractures which may not affect his life expectancy or there is no evidence that he died on account of the injuries sustained in the accident.
No post-mortem examination was conducted, death was not reported to the police and no medical officer was examined before the Tribunal to say that the death was on account of the injuries.
In spite of the contest, the Tribunal has awarded compensation under loss of estate, funeral and transportation expenses, loss of consortium, mental shock and agony.
At the most, the legal representatives are entitled to claim medical expenses incurred.
The mode of assessment of loss of estate is done considering the age, income of the deceased and by applying the multiplier.
The entire loss of dependency is awarded as loss of estate, which is contrary to law and has sought for interference.

7. Per contra, learned counsel for the legal representatives of Hanumantha Gouda, who are the NC:
2024:KHC-D:7967 petitioners, has contended that the son of the deceased Hanumantha Gouda and one independent witness examined as PWs.2 and 3 respectively.
The deceased had suffered fracture of right tibia and fibula, fracture of right forearm, fracture of three left ribs and fracture of two right ribs.
He was under hospitalization for a period of two months and also has taken follow up treatment.

A sum of Rs.1,30,802/- was spent towards medical expenses and the death was on account of the injuries only and thereby the petitioners are entitled to claim loss of estate and medical expenses and other incidental expenses including loss of dependency and the Tribunal has rightly considered the same and supported the impugned judgment.

8. In support of his contention, learned counsel has relied upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of The Oriental Insurance Company Limited Vs. Kahlon @ Jasmail Singh Kahlon (deceased) NC: 2024:KHC-D:7967 through his legal representatives Narinder Kahlon Gosakan and Another1.
9.

sentences.text: I gave my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed by both the parties and perused the records.

entities.text: Iffco Tokio General Insurance Co., Ltd vs Hanumantha Gouda
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no dispute that there was an accident on 18.02.2008 involving a Tom Tom and a motorcycle, in which Hanumantha Gouda was the pillion rider.

He sustained injuries to his right leg,
right forearm and ribs.
He was under hospitalization for one month.
Hanumantha Gouda filed the claim petition seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in the accident.
The claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.
During the pendancy of the proceedings, Hanumantha Gouda died and his wife and sons are brought on record as the legal representatives.
It is their case that Hanumantha Gouda had died on account of the injuries.
(2021) 8 S.C.R. 469 NC: 2024:KHC-D:7967 11. It is pertinent to note that, on 25.02.2009, Hanumantha Gouda died one year after the accident.
He was under hospitalization from 18.02.2008 to 23.03.2008 i.e., around one month.
After the death of Hanumantha Gouda, death was not reported to the police nor any post- mortem examination was conducted on the dead body of Hanumantha Gouda.
Though petitioners claim that Hanumantha Gouda died on account of injuries, except the testimony of PW2 - son and PW3 - independent eyewitness, no medical evidence is placed.
PWs. 2 and 3 are rustic villagers.
They were fully dependent on medical records.
As mentioned above, the nature of injuries sustained by Hanumantha Gouda are the fractures and these fractures are not on the vital part of the body.

One month after the discharge, though they claim that follow up was taken at SDM Medical Hospital,
Dharwad, prescription bills show that they are all relevant to the time of treatment during the hospitalization.

No medical evidence is placed to show that Hanumantha Gouda was under follow up treatment, he was in such a condition that NC: 2024:KHC-D:7967 his death is directly related to the injuries sustained by him.
12. I have carefully perused the impugned judgment.
The Tribunal has not given any reason how Hanumantha Gouda had died.
There is no evidence on record to connect the nexus between the injuries to the death of the deceased Hanumantha Gouda.

Hence it is not proper on the part of the Tribunal to award compensation towards loss of estate, funeral and transportation expenses and loss of consortium to the wife including mental shock and agony.
At the most, the petitioners are entitled to reimbursement of medical expenses and incidental expenses towards the treatment.

13. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Kahlon @ Jasmail Singh Kahlon's case (supra), while dealing with an injured person was under prolonged hospitalization for six months, at para 17 of the judgment held that, the extent of disability suffered was 100%, after treatment it was reduced to 75% and the injuries made him to resign from - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:7967 his job.
He was in such a condition that movement was difficult and without an attendant, he cannot do anything and he was with complete immobility.
Under such circumstances, the Hon'ble Apex Court held that the death was on account of the injuries sustained and the legal representatives are entitled to loss of estate on account of death.

Iffco Tokio General Insurance Co., Ltd vs Hanumantha Gouda S/O. Sangana Gouda on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73282535/
4 14.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case, the accident was on 18.02.2008.
The injured was discharged from the hospital on 25.03.2008, after one month of treatment.
Ex . P25
is the inpatient record, which shows the injured was under hospitalization up to 25.03.2008 for a period of one month.
No evidence is placed to show nexus between the injuries to the death.
Hence, above principles is not helpful to the petitioners herein.
15. The petitioners being the wife and sons, have spent money towards treatment of deceased Hanumantha Gouda.
They have also spent money towards attendant charges, traveling, food and nourishment and therefore - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:7967 they have to be compensated accordingly.
The medical bills itself amounts to Rs.1,30,802/-, which has to be reimbursed.
The deceased was inpatient for about two months and hence taking the income at the rate of Rs.4,250/- per month, loss of income during laid up period of two months has to be assessed at Rs.8,500/-.
The traveling expenses assessed at Rs.2,000/- and during the hospitalization, food and nourishment is assessed at Rs.8,000/-.
Thereby, the petitioners are entitled to a total compensation of Rs,1,49,302/- as against Rs.6,30,802/- assessed by the Tribunal.
16. Hence, the appeal merits consideration.

In the result, the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed in part.
ii. The judgment and award dated 30.07.2011 passed in MVC No.100/2009 by the Addl. MACT - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:7967 and Fast Track Court-II, Koppal, stands modified.
iii. The petitioners are entitled to compensation of Rs.1,49,302/- in stead of Rs.6,70,802/- awarded by the Tribunal, thereby reduction of Rs.5,21,500/-.
iv. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount within eight weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the Tribunal for disbursement forthwith.

Sd/-
